answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a rugged umber grid to enforce physical presence. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates acting as a stationary island anchor, and each receipt proves an agent physically occupied the site. A verifier functions as a marble-hard fault detector, replaying logs to detect latency shifts; any discrepancy beyond the noise floor triggers a permanent penalty. Honest nodes pay linear travel costs, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion and immediate banishment.
